summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and completed his doctorate under Muni Jinvijaya. He served as professor at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1945–1965) and directed the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi specializes in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University before holding the chair of Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia (~1987–2021).
Harogadde Manappa Nayak worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1984) and later as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin was a linguist and scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and Yale University. He held academic posts at Columbia University and Yale University (1962–1996), also serving as Curator of Anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

Harold Edward Musson worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, and under traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana. Earlier, he served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed his doctorate at McMaster University. He held positions at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992), including directing its press (1981–1983), and directed at the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

Harold Hargreaves was an Indologist and archaeologist. After serving as headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar, he served extensively with the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent and Deputy Director General between 1910 and 1931.

Harold Herman Bender worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lafayette College, Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and Berlin under Richard Pischel and Wilhelm Schulze. He was an assistant professor at Princeton University (1909–1950).

Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. After teaching at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he served as a professor of humanities at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2008).
Harold Stewart was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney (~1939–1941).

Harold Walter Bailey worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Western Australia and Oxford, he taught Iranian studies at SOAS (1929–1936) and held the Sanskrit chair at the University of Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University and the University of Oxford, and was mentored by Ghulam Yazdani. He held posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).

Harry Campbell Norman was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh under Samuel Henry Butcher, William Ross Hardie, and Julius Eggeling, and at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. In 1905, he was appointed Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Harry Charles Purvis Bell was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at Cheltenham College in 1864 and joined the Ceylon Civil Service in 1873.

Harry Falk is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ulrich Schneider and Gaya Charan Tripathi. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1980–1990) and the Free University of Berlin (1993–2012), where he served as Director.
Harry Halén is a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Pentti Aalto (~1968–1975). He served as an amanuensis at the University of Helsinki (~1971–2008).

Harsha Gautam is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Texas at Austin, where she also worked as a teaching assistant, later becoming a fellow at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

Harshit Mishra works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi, Central Sanskrit University, Ghent University, and the International School for Jain Studies, where he also served as a research associate in 2024.

Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Weller and completed his doctorate under Paul Thieme. He held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.
